notes:
**Placeholder text hiding in your search snippet is now found.**

Every text check in Docket read a page's rendered body. The meta description, the `og:description` and a JSON-LD `description` are a second copy of the same sentence — and they are the copy Google and an AI crawler quote first. Nothing was reading them.

So a site could ship *"Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet"* as the sentence that appears under its own name in search results, and Docket would call the page clean.

It now checks that surface too, and says which one it found, because the fix is different: edit the tag, not the copy. A page that *argues against* placeholder text in its description is still left alone, and a page carrying filler in both its body and its meta is reported once.
